issues.claim: Missed subject: the view-bound why for section providers. The why card's `plan` damage rows are read at the view's drawn week. V03 §5.6 (2) (d) (l. 2718–2721) says `own` serves 'the `plan` section's rows (V03 §4.6) … The week is the drawn week of the view or the export (§2.9's `week`; a scrubbed frame's, V06 §3.15.2), so scrubbing history shows one plan aging'. V09 §2.12's damage-lines row (l. 1010) derives them 'at V06's `decayLevel` for the drawn week' for 'the plan panel; the why card's `plan` section'. V09 §4.21.13 (1) and V10 §3.9a's `info.damage.head.<state>` row (l. 1838) give 'the whole years of its decay run at the drawn week'. The rows come from V03 §4.6's `plan` `WhySectionProvider` (l. 2377–2387: 'read from `PlanDamage` at the own level'), and `planDamage(doc, b, plan, view: ViewState, opts)` needs a view. But V10 §2.13 types the section provider as `rows(model: ModelView, id: Id, key: Knowledge)` (l. 990), with no view and no week. R4-05 gave the view only to the kind's `WhyProvider.explain` (`opts.view`), and neither §11.2's `why` comment (l. 16288–16290) nor V10 §3.9's query (l. 1642–1645, 'then appends the rows of every registered `WhySectionProvider`') passes anything to the sections. So an input that V03, V09 and V10 name has no producer. At a scrubbed week — a normal timeline path (V06 §3.15.2) — the plan panel shows that week's damage. One builder of the provider reads the document's current week; another cannot build the call. The card's 'Inside' section and the clerk's damage answer then differ from the panel beside them. T-V9-86 and T-V10-53 run at the head only.
issues.required_change: (1) §11.2's `why` member (l. 16288–16290), after '… a provider that states no view's look ignores it': add '; a section provider whose rows are read at the drawn week — V03 §4.6's `plan` damage rows (V03 §5.6 (2) (d)) — reads that view's `week`, and with no view the document's current week (§2.9's `week` default)'. (2) END at V10 §2.13 (l. 989–990): `rows(model: ModelView, id: Id, key: Knowledge): WhySection['rows']` → `rows(model: ModelView, id: Id, key: Knowledge, opts: { view?: WhyProvider's opts.view /* the same view the kind's provider is passed (§11.2's view-bound why); a section whose rows read the drawn week — V03 §4.6's plan damage rows — reads view.week, else the document's current week */ }): WhySection['rows']`. (3) END at V10 §3.9's query paragraph (l. 1644): 'then appends the rows of every registered `WhySectionProvider` whose `appliesTo` holds' adds '— each passed the same `opts.view` —'. (4) END at V10 §3.23 row 14: the no-view outcome adds 'the `plan` section's damage rows at the document's current week'. (5) END at V03 §4.6's `plan` damage rows (l. 2377–2378): 'read from `PlanDamage` at the own level (V03 §5.6 (2) (d))' adds 'at the why's view's drawn week (`opts.view.week`, V10 §2.13; §11.2's view-bound `why`), else the document's current week'. (6) END at V09: T-V9-86 adds 'at a scrubbed week (V06 §3.15.2) the why card's `plan` section shows that week's own-level lines and head years, as the plan panel does'.

issues.claim: A picture export draws a map's pins by default in one unit and never by default in the other. V09 §5.10's Picture tab (l. 4037) offers 'pins and public notes on · off (off by default)'. V09's entity table (l. 4137) says pins are 'never in pictures unless "Show pins" is on in the Picture tab'. §11.2's `ExportOpts` claims to declare 'every option an export reads … written by V09 §5.10's dialog' (l. 16197–16198) but has no member for that option. Its `furniture` is 'the picture's furniture (§9.5): default true' (l. 16219). §9.5's furniture list includes the Annotation layer ('numbered markers and a separate legend sheet', l. 15067). The measure tool's result 'can be saved as an annotation', which V09 §4.19 writes as a view pin ('Save as annotation writes a view pin labelled with the measure'). So an exporter built from §11.2 draws the view pins in every default picture. V09 offers the opposite default, and its switch has no member to carry it. This is two units with two outcomes for one case (a picture of a map holding pins), the class R3-03 grades major; the missing member is also VRC2T-12's class.
issues.required_change: (1) §11.2's `ExportOpts`, after `furniture?`, adds `pins?: boolean;   // a picture (PNG, SVG, print): §9.5's annotation layer — the view pins and public notes (§2.9; V09 §4.19), drawn as the view draws them — over the map with the furniture; default false (V09 §5.10's "pins and public notes": never in a picture unless asked)`. `furniture?`'s comment reads 'the picture's furniture (§9.5), the annotation layer excepted (`pins`): default true'. (2) §9.5's *Annotation layer* bullet adds '(the view pins, §2.9; V09 §4.19 — in a picture only with `ExportOpts.pins`, §11.2)'. (3) END at V09: l. 4137's 'never in pictures unless "Show pins" is on in the Picture tab' → 'never in pictures unless the Picture tab's **pins and public notes** is on (§11.2's `ExportOpts.pins`)'; §5.10's Picture options cell 'pins and public notes on · off (off by default)' adds '(`ExportOpts.pins`)'. (4) T-ER-19 adds 'a picture of a map holding view pins with `pins` absent and true: no annotation drawn, then every pin drawn'.

issues.claim: V10 restates Find at a drawn week in the form R4-12 superseded. R4-12 amended R3-24's 'restricted to the entities that frame holds' to §11.2's frame listing (l. 16455–16464: 'a building matches by its use at that week, never its head use, and an entity or use the frame holds matches though the head has since closed, moved or demolished it'), and V09 §4.21.10 (8) now reads so. V10 keeps the old form at three sites: §3.9b (7) (l. 2002–2005) 'each chip counts, lists and gaps only the entities that frame holds'; §3.23 row 32 'each chip counted, listed and gapped over that frame's entities alone'; T-V10-51 'they equal the panel's over that frame's entities'. `read_map find` reads §11.2's gazetteer with `week`, so nothing built changes; the prose is a narrower restatement.
issues.required_change: V10 §3.9b (7): 'each chip counts, lists and gaps only the entities that frame holds — a chip with none there counting 0 for that week' → 'each chip counts, lists and gaps §11.2's listing at that week — the frame's matches, by the uses it holds open then, so a building matches by its use at that week, never its head use — a chip with none there counting 0 for that week'. §3.23 row 32: the outcome 'each chip counted, listed and gapped over that frame's entities alone' → 'each chip counted, listed and gapped by §11.2's listing at that week (the frame's matches, a building by its use then)'; its edge '(a scrub to before a matched building was built)' adds 'or before a matched building's use changed'. T-V10-51: 'they equal the panel's over that frame's entities' → 'they equal the panel's — §11.2's listing at that week, a building matched by its use then'.

issues.claim: V09 §4.21.13 (2) (l. 3697–3699) gives the restored case as 'an element the plan gained after its damage left is drawn as built (V06 §3.23 (3)'s per-element peak)', and row 92 (l. 1612) has 'a restored building, re-cut or extended after its repair' with the same outcome. R4-03 adds a second case: an element a restoring event's re-cut mints is drawn as built while that restoration runs and is never patched. It is written at V03 §5.6 (2) (l. 2702–2706: 'or minted by a restoring re-cut, is drawn as built — never damaged by that restoration nor repaired'), at model §2.6 step 7 and at V10 §3.9a (l. 1855–1856: 'or that a restoring re-cut minted, never among them'). R4-03's sweep did not name V09, so V09's twin of V10's sentence keeps the narrower form. V09 draws through V03's `planDamage`, so nothing built changes.
issues.required_change: V09 §4.21.13 (2): 'and an element the plan gained after its damage left is drawn as built (V06 §3.23 (3)'s per-element peak)' → 'and an element the plan gained after its damage left, or that a restoring event's re-cut minted, is drawn as built — never damaged by that restoration nor patched (V03 §5.6 (2); V06 §3.23 (3))'. Row 92: the edge 'a restored building, re-cut or extended after its repair' adds 'or re-cut by its restoring event while its `repair` Works runs'; the outcome 'an element the plan gained after its damage left drawn as built (V06 §3.23 (3))' → 'an element the plan gained after its damage left, or a restoring re-cut minted, drawn as built (V06 §3.23 (3))'.
